claims.text: Enhanced surface segregation lowers the local cohesive energy at HEA nanoparticle surfaces.
Enhanced surface segregation lowers the local surface energy at HEA nanoparticle surfaces.
Surface segregation reduces the onset temperature for premelting relative to a randomized surface composition.
The baseline HEA nanoparticles have a randomized, well-mixed surface atomic distribution.
A mild annealing or chemical segregation protocol can induce controlled surface segregation while bulk composition, particle size, support, and other processing conditions are held constant.
The degree of surface atomic segregation alters local cohesive energies.
The degree of surface atomic segregation alters local surface energies.
Surface segregation concentrates lower-cohesive-energy elements at the nanoparticle surface.
Concentrating lower-cohesive-energy elements at the surface reduces the energy barrier for atomic rearrangements.
The reduced barrier for surface atomic rearrangements initiates premelting at a lower temperature.
Pre-segregated nanoparticles will exhibit a lower premelting temperature than randomized-surface nanoparticles.
Pre-segregated nanoparticles will exhibit an earlier and possibly more gradual melting transition than the randomized baseline.
The proposed segregation effect should persist from premelting onset through complete melting when particle size and support interactions are controlled.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature shift may depend on elemental composition.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature shift may depend on segregation extent.
Support interactions and particle-size variations may influence premelting behavior.
A controlled thermal-ramp comparison using DSC, in situ TEM, and surface-composition analysis can test whether segregation changes premelting onset and melting kinetics.

Failure to observe either a statistically significant reduction in premelting temperature or altered melting kinetics in the segregated batch would falsify surface segregation as the governing factor.
